How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Electronic submission of Public Comment is also available via the City’s website as
noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically will be read into the record.
Words that would disrupt the meeting, including profanity, obscenity, and
discriminatory language, will not be read. Your comments must be received by 5:00
P.M. on meeting day.

Website: Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
  Public Comment.

   City Council Regular Meeting Agenda
  Tuesday, June 18, 2024

 •  CALL TO ORDER
 •  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE LED BY: Vice Mayor Menchaca
 •  ROLL CALL: Mayor Wu, Vice Mayor Menchaca, Council Members Chan, Ding,
  Harrington

 1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

 2. PRESENTATIONS

  A. JUNETEENTH DAY

 3. PUBLIC COMMENT

 4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  All items listed under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and
  recommendations will be approved in one motion unless a member of the
  City Council or audience requests separate discussion.

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The minutes are a record of the official actions taken at the City Council
  meeting.

  1. Minutes of the City Council Special Meeting of June 4, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the City Council Regular Meeting of June 4, 2024.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action: Approval

  B. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented
  to the City Council for review and approval.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  2
   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as
  presented.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – MAY 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2023-2024 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 23-36) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment
  Report is presented to receive and file in accordance with the City’s adopted
  2023-2024 Investment Policy.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for May 2024.

  D. ATHENS SERVICES REQUEST FOR ANNUAL RATE REVIEW AND
  ADJUSTMENTS FOR WASTE SERVICES AND STREET SWEEPING SERVICES
  AT A MONTHLY COST OF $11,097.67

  In accordance with the Sixth Amendment to the contract for services dated July
  6, 2021, Athens Services has submitted two requests for City Council’s approval
  to adjust the rates for street sweeping and waste services in accordance with
  applicable Consumer Price Indices to take effect on July 1, 2024. The annual
  budget for street sweeping services is $133,172.04 and is included in the Fiscal
  Year 2024-2025 budget and will be funded by Gas Tax account 136-800-02-22-
  055.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the annual rate adjustments proposed by Athens Services rate
  schedules that take effect on July 1, 2024; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  3
   2. Authorize the City Manager to approve a purchase order with Athens
  Services for $133,172.04 for street sweeping services using the Gas Tax
  account 136-800-02-22-055.

  E. PURCHASE OF A FIRE DEPARTMENT STAFF VEHICLE IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $71,110

  The San Gabriel Fire Department utilizes a variety of vehicles in its fleet to meet
  emergency response and administrative responsibilities. The proposed new
  vehicle will replace a 2004 Chevrolet Tahoe that has more than 215,000 miles
  and has served as the primary emergency vehicle for the past five Fire Chiefs,
  Fire Prevention, and is currently assigned to a Division Chief. The 2004 vehicle
  will be returned to the Fleet Department for re-assignment or removal from
  inventory subject to City of San Gabriel policy. The total purchase price of the
  vehicle, including tax, documentation and delivery is $71,110.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to issue a
  purchase order in the amount of $71,110 to Rotolo Chevrolet for the purchase
  of one new Chevrolet Tahoe LT.

  F. UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA, LOS ANGELES (UCLA) CENTER FOR
  PREHOSPITAL CARE CONTRACT

  The San Gabriel Fire Department is required as an Advanced Life Support
  provider in the County of Los Angeles, to maintain an approved Continuing
  Education and Quality Assurance Program. In 2014, University of California, Los
  Angeles (UCLA) was contracted to provide these services for a five-year term.
  Two contract extensions have been previously approved, and the current
  agreement is scheduled to expire on July 31, 2024. The proposed new contract
  provides for service until August 1, 2029. The total of $41,760 per year is billed
  at a monthly rate of $3,480. The new rate represents an increase of
  approximately 28% over the previous agreement of $32,769 annually. Under
  terms of the new agreement, UCLA may increase at an annual rate of no more
  than 5% per year to cover any increases in cost for services, which has been the
  standard escalator cap since the inception of the contract. Funding for this
  contract is budgeted in the 121-761-22-00-000 contractual services account.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager or Fire Chief
  to enter into the new Contract for Services Agreement with the UCLA Center
  for Prehospital Care in the amount of $41,760 annually for the duration of the
  agreement.

  G. ACCEPTANCE OF 2020 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY  PROGRAM
  SUPPLEMENTAL GRANT AWARD [RESOLUTION NO. 24-37]

  The San Gabriel Fire Department (SGFD) has been awarded supplemental
  funding from the 2020 State Homeland Security Program in the amount of
  $44,257. The SGFD can use these funds to finance purchases from the
  Department of Homeland Security Approved Equipment List. Initial outlay is up
  to $44,257, and will be fully reimbursed, with no matching funds due from the
  City of San Gabriel. The deadline to use these funds is July 5, 2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-37 approving
  the following:
  1. Increase account 186-3215 by $44,257 (revenue account).

  2. Increase the Fire Department Fiscal Year 2023-2024 budget by $44,257 in
  account 124-761-57-99-380.
  3. Authorize the City Manager or Fire Chief to accept the State Homeland
  Security Program supplemental grant and purchase items from the
  Department of Homeland Security Approved Equipment List under the
  City’s purchasing policy.

  H. APPROVAL OF LA LAGUNA DE SAN GABRIEL REHABILITATION PROJECT
  AND ACCEPTANCE OF NOTICE OF EXEMPTION

  On May 16, 2023, the City Council approved the grant funds from
  Assemblymember Fong for a rehabilitation project for various structures of La
  Laguna de San Gabriel. In order to complete the required state application for
  the receipt of the funds, California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA)

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  5
   determination is required and final approval of the project by the Council. The
  filing of the Notice of Exemption determination is $75. Since the rehabilitation
  work was completed on a City resource, the fee will be covered by the
  Community Services budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The rehabilitation
  project completed at La Laguna is exempt from the requirements of CEQA, per
  Guidelines 15331, Class 31.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Find the project is exempt from CEQA pursuant to CEQA Guidelines Section
  15331 and authorize the City Manager to file the Notice of Exemption; and
  2. Approve the rehabilitation project.

  I. UPDATED FACILITIES JOINT AGREEMENT WITH SAN GABRIEL UNIFIED
  SCHOOL DISTRICT AND REQUEST FOR AUTHORIZATION TO FUND A
  PORTION OF THE PLAYGROUND CONSTRUCTION COSTS FOR COOLIDGE
  SCHOOL PARK FROM PARK DEVELOPMENT IMPACT FEES IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $100,000

  On September 20, 2022, the City Council approved the Amended and Restated
  Facilities Joint Use Agreement with the San Gabriel Unified School District. The
  term of the amended agreement was from August 1, 2022 to July 31, 2027. Due
  to various changes in maintenance and facility usage, staff is bringing the
  agreement forward for City Council approval. Approval of financial support of
  $100,000 in park development impact fees account 124-850-40-97-807 is
  recommended to contribute to the construction of a playground at Coolidge
  School Park.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Review and approve the proposed Amended and Restates Facilities Joint
  Use Agreement; and authorize the City Manager and Mayor to execute the
  agreement; and

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  6
   2. Authorize the recommended amount of $100,000 in park impact fees
  account 124-850-40-97-807 to contribute to the construction of a
  playground at Coolidge School Park.

  J. APPROVAL OF MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH SAN GABRIEL
  UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT FOR USE OF GABRIELINO HIGH SCHOOL
  CAMPUS FOR INDEPENDENCE DAY CELEBRATION

  The City of San Gabriel will hold its Independence Day Celebration on
  Wednesday, July 3, 2024. The event will include entertainment, games, food
  trucks and will end with a drone show. The Independence Day Celebration will
  be held at Gabrielino High School. Any custodial work needed for the City’s use
  of the property will be billed at $40 per hour. This amount will be covered by
  the Non-Departmental account for special events.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The rehabilitation
  project completed at La Laguna is exempt from the requirements of CEQA, per
  Guidelines 15331, Class 31.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Gabrielino High School as the location for the Independence Day
  Celebration; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to sign the Memorandum of Understanding
  with San Gabriel Unified School District for this purpose.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING

  A. ADOPT ORDINANCE NO. 708 ADDING SECTION 150.300 TO THE CITY OF
  SAN GABRIEL MUNICIPAL CODE SETTING FORTH AN EXPEDITED,
  STREAMLINED PERMITTING PROCESS FOR ELECTRIC VEHICLE CHARGING
  STATIONS AS REQUIRED BY GOVERNMENT CODE SECTION 65850.7. –
  SECOND READING AND ADOPTION

  Ordinance No. 708 was approved at introduction by a 5-0 vote of the City
  Council at the June 4, 2024 City Council meeting. If adopted, Ordinance No. 708
  would add Section 150.300 to the City of San Gabriel Municipal Code, setting
  forth an expedited, streamlined permitting process for electric vehicle charging
  stations as required by the State of California Government Code Section
  65870.7. By streamlining the permitting process represents a proactive step in

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  7
   compliance with California State Assembly Bill 1236. There is no fiscal impact
  related to this item.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Conduct the public hearing and discuss the proposed Ordinance No. 708.

  2. Waive reading and adopt Ordinance No. 708: An Ordinance of the City
  Council of the City of San Gabriel, California, Setting Forth Procedures for
  Expediting Permitting Processing for Electric Vehicle Charging Systems.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS – None.

 7. NEW BUSINESS

  A. APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH ARTS CONSULTING GROUP IN THE
  AMOUNT OF $18,000 TO CONDUCT A MISSION PLAYHOUSE STRATEGIC
  VISIONING WORKSHOP

  In fall of 2020, the City Council reviewed organizational changes for the Mission
  Playhouse. At that time, it was clear that the Council valued the Playhouse as a
  historic gem and wanted to maintain management by the City. As a next step
  and movement toward fundraising for the 100th Anniversary of the theater, staff
  is seeking to hire Arts Consulting Group (ACG) to conduct a strategic visioning
  exercise for the Playhouse to help focus the fundraising goals for the City
  including the possible development of a non-profit. ACG’s fee for the proposed
  workshop, gathering background information, a comparison study, and
  stakeholder survey is $16,000 with estimated travel, transport, meals cost of
  $2,000 for a total of $18,000. Staff is proposing to cover the cost of this with
  the approved Fiscal Year 2024-2025 Mission Playhouse operating budget,
  reallocated into the Special Project account 124-712-35-96-819.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – June 18, 2024  8
   1. Approve a contract with Arts Consulting Group to conduct the Mission
  Playhouse Visioning Workshop; and

  2. Utilizing the City’s standard consultant contract, authorize the City Manager
  to execute the contract and any other necessary documents pending review
  and approval by the City Attorney.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT

  9. CITY MANAGER’S REPORT

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Each Council Member may address the City Council and public on matters of
  general information and/or concern. This is also the time for Council Members to
  report on conferences and/or meetings they have attended.

  11. CLOSED SESSION – None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The next regular City Council meeting will be held on Tuesday, July 2, 2024 at
  6:30 P.M. Information regarding matters to be considered at each meeting will be
  available on the Friday before the City Council Meeting on the City’s website at
  www.sangabrielcity.com.

MINUTES OF JUNE 18, 2024
  REGULAR MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the regular meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 6:31 P.M.

  San Gabriel, California, 91776.

I  Chief City Clerk Sharon Clark, Public Works Director/City
